name: GM - Lansing Grand River Assembly, Lansing MI

fieldNotes.facility: Positively identified GM Lansing Grand River Assembly (LGR), 920 Townsend St. Coords from Wikipedia (42 deg 43'22"N 84 deg 33'42"W = 42.7228,-84.5617) land on a 3.4M-sq-ft integrated assembly+stamping complex on the Grand River, between I-496 (N) and the river/rail (S). Confirmed in satellite: one continuous fenced manufacturing campus, finished-vehicle marshaling lots, internal trailer staging, conveyor/ped bridges between buildings. Verlinden Ave Street View (2025-07) shows the plant wall + perimeter fence + a signalized controlled intersection at the truck entrance.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Fully fenced controlled-access GM assembly plant. Street View on Verlinden Ave shows continuous chain-link/wall perimeter fencing and a signalized gated intersection at the truck entry; satellite shows internal lane markings and a controlled pinch-point where the main drive meets the building courtyard.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Standard for an integrated GM assembly plant of this scale; controlled gates with security booths at the truck/employee entrances (guarded campus). Booth-scale structures present at the main entries.
fieldNotes.entryExitSeparate: Large campus with multiple gates: a north/visitor entry off the office side and a separate freight/employee entry on the Verlinden/courtyard side; in and out flows split across gates.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide gate aprons and multi-lane internal drives with unused paved width; physical room to add a JIT express/bypass lane for the high-frequency inbound supplier trailers.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Paved internal courtyards and lanes inside the fence between the gate and the dock faces provide trailer queueing/holding before docks.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Estimate ~45 from overhead imagery; docks are distributed across multiple connected building faces and internal courtyards (assembly, body, stamping, logistics center), some tucked between building masses, so band 25-50 is the honest call.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Trailer drop/staging seen in the west-central lot near the dirt parcel (8-10 trailers staged) plus trailer rows near the SW rail/river edge; banded 25-50 across the site.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer-storage / drop lots present (west-central paved lot with parked trailers, and SW trailer/container staging beside the rail spur), separate from active dock staging.
fieldNotes.railServed: Active rail line runs along the south/SW edge of the property on the Grand River bank with a spur and rail-served trailer/container staging visible; GM operates an inbound logistics/sequencing center at LGR (corroborated by Automotive Logistics and GM facility pages).
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Integrated campus: body shop, paint, general assembly, an on-site stamping plant, and a $44.5M logistics optimization/sequencing center, all on the one 111-acre property.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Inside the City of Lansing dense urban fabric, surrounded by residential neighborhoods, downtown, and the river; clearly Urban.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale clearly identified in imagery; left uncertain.
fieldNotes.multiStep: Plausible outer-gate-then-internal-checkpoint flow on a guarded auto campus, but not clearly resolvable in imagery; left false and flagged.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: 111 acres per GM/Wikipedia; perimeter ring traced to the fenced footprint between I-496, Verlinden/Townsend, and the Grand River/rail edge.
fieldNotes.streetViewMeta: Best ground view is the Verlinden Ave road pano at 42.72552,-84.56047 (captured 2025-07) looking E (~95 deg) toward the plant wall, fence, and the controlled truck-entry intersection; pano id not captured in this pass.
